column1: # One case per line: flags <TAB> pattern <TAB> subject.
# Nothing here says what the right answer is. tools/regex-test.sh runs
# each case through this project's engine and through the host's own
# <regex.h>, and they must agree - offsets of the whole match and of
# every captured group, or "nomatch", or "error". That is the only
# useful standard for a program whose entire job is to decide the same
# flags: E extended (ERE)  I icase  N newline  S nosub
#        b notbol  e noteol      (empty means basic, BRE)
# In the subject, \n means a real newline.
# ---- BRE groups and backreferences, which no automaton can do
# ---- leftmost-longest, which is where a Perl-style engine disagrees
# ---- two cases deliberately NOT graded, and why
# POSIX leaves both of these undefined or ambiguous, so the host's answer
# is one conforming answer rather than the right one, and a differential
# test cannot grade a question with two correct answers. Each is listed
# here with the choice this engine makes, so that "not tested" does not
# An empty pattern. POSIX: "the use of an empty BRE/ERE is undefined."
# The host's engine rejects it; this one accepts it and matches the empty
# string at position 0. Chosen deliberately: `grep ""` is a thing people
# type and a thing scripts generate, and matching every line is far more
# useful than an error. See regex.h.
#   # A backreference under REG_ICASE. The host compares the referenced text
# case-sensitively even with ICASE on; this engine folds, so \1 matches
# "A" after \(a\) matched "a". Chosen because REG_ICASE says to ignore
# case when matching and a backreference is matching. See regex.h.
# ---- errors: each must be rejected by both
